CUMULATIVE COMPARISON

Costs, tax relief, and exit liability

Pre-exit tax relief is already reflected in the cash account; do not add it to wealth again. Incremental exit tax is the change in the final-year tax bill when the full sale is included. Unused loss carryforwards have no terminal cash value.

METHOD

Three strategies, one comparison

Index The benchmark

A low-cost index strategy used as the benchmark. No intentional tax-loss harvesting.

Long-only DI Direct indexing

Holds individual stocks and realizes losses that may offset capital gains. Its loss curve here is an illustrative assumption.

Core 130/30 Long-short investing

For each $100 of net capital, holds $130 long and $30 short. The model includes financing, rebates, borrowing costs, and loss offsets.

Sources, assumptions, and what is still missing

Core loss curve: 15%, 10%, 7%, 4%, then 2% annually for Years 5-10, applied to beginning-of-year NAV. These are independent illustrative assumptions, not provider estimates or observed account losses.

Restricted course run: The original source-based configuration and workbook are available separately through the course data link. Use the reproduction instructions in docs/RESTRICTED_DATA.md; this browser example uses the public inputs.

Long-only DI: The illustrative loss curve is 5%, 3%, 2%, 1%, 0.5%, then 0.3% annually. It has not been calibrated to historical data. Index has no intentional harvesting.

Fixed assumptions: Index / DI management fees are 0.03% / 0.25%. Annual trading cost rates for Index / DI / Core are 0 / 0.03% / 0.05%; exit trading rates are 0.01% / 0.01% / 0.02% of gross exposure. Side cash earns 0%; there are no dividends or alpha. Interest deductions are capped at modeled rebate income; fees are not given a blanket tax deduction.

Tax simplifications: Losses offset gains of the same character first, then the other character; unused losses carry forward. All realizations at exactly one year are ST. Later, assumed ST shares for Index / DI / Core are 0% / 5% / 10%. Individual brackets, state tax details, and capital-loss deductions against ordinary income are omitted.

Not yet included: Observed market prices, individual tax lots, wash-sale checks, actual trades, margin calls, and calibrated risk estimates. Return paths and loss curves are independent assumptions; the model does not establish that these losses can be realized in practice.

This first-stage scenario model supports accounting checks and discussion of assumptions. It does not establish suitability for a real client. Full inputs and source notes are in scenario.json in the download and in the original Python project documentation.
